# pgvector — Vector Similarity Search for AI

pgvector adds a `vector` type for storing and searching AI embeddings — essential for RAG (Retrieval Augmented Generation) and semantic search.

## Setup

```sql
CREATE EXTENSION vector;
```

## Basic Usage

```sql
-- Create a table with a vector column
CREATE TABLE documents (
    id BIGINT PRIMARY KEY,
    content TEXT NOT NULL,
    embedding VECTOR(1536)  -- OpenAI text-embedding-ada-002 dimension
);

-- Insert (embedding generated by your AI model)
INSERT INTO documents (id, content, embedding)
VALUES (1, 'PostgreSQL is great', '[0.1, 0.2, 0.3, ...]');

-- Find the 5 most similar documents
SELECT id, content, embedding <=> '[0.1, 0.2, 0.3, ...]' AS distance
FROM documents
ORDER BY embedding <=> '[0.1, 0.2, 0.3, ...]'
LIMIT 5;
```

## Distance Operators

| Operator | Metric | Use Case |
|----------|--------|----------|
| `<->` | L2 (Euclidean) distance | Image similarity |
| `<=>` | Cosine distance | Text similarity (most common) |
| `<#>` | Negative inner product | When vectors are normalized |

## Indexing

```sql
-- HNSW index (recommended — best recall/speed)
CREATE INDEX ON documents USING hnsw (embedding vector_cosine_ops)
WITH (m = 16, ef_construction = 64);

-- IVFFlat index (faster build, less recall)
CREATE INDEX ON documents USING ivfflat (embedding vector_cosine_ops)
WITH (lists = 100);

-- Tune search at runtime
SET hnsw.ef_search = 40;  -- higher = better recall, slower
```

## RAG Pattern (Retrieval Augmented Generation)

```sql
-- 1. User asks a question
-- 2. Generate embedding of the question using your AI model
-- 3. Find similar documents
SELECT content FROM documents
ORDER BY embedding <=> $1  -- $1 = question embedding
LIMIT 5;

-- 4. Feed the retrieved documents + question to your LLM
```
